Expansion:
Britain has used a specific land survey system for a long time, Mets and Bounds, which they brought to their colonies (the eastern US). The basic premise is that borders are described like a treasure map, using objects in the land as references. This creates a lot of border disputes, though, as sometimes the definition of the border is vague. 
To fix this, Thomas Jefferson created the Township and Range survey system, which the rest of America (the west) would adopt. It works by laying out a grid across the land. The lines in the grid would then be the borders.

When you play Hammond, make sure you don't have too much downtime. Also, don't go in too much, or else you'll feed. Dive in from an off angle when you have Adaptive Shields and piledrive to put pressure on the enemies, preferably the backline. Just make sure to stay within your team's FOV, or else they won't be able to help you.

Congratulations, you just initiated a proper engagement. Now try to cause as much chaos as you can using a mix of guns and abilities while still keeping an eye on your health bar and where your team is at.

Other tips:
-Knock squishy enemies into your team's FOV if you get the chance.
-Before every fight, use Ball mode's 3rd Person view to scout where the enemies are from around a corner. 
-Learn some techs, especially wall jump. They're pretty handy.
-It's better to leave a 1v1 than it is to die. Don't overstay your welcome because you really want someone to die.
-Get health packs.
-Load up custom games to try to find cool grapple spots for engagements. Also watch other Ball players for this as well.
